added: While most newer model cars have done much to hide the wiring and otherwise outfit the steering column with safety measures to prevent hot-wiring, older models up to the mid-90s are typically good candidates for hot-wiring. This is important to know if you lose your [[Replace Car Keys|keys]] and need to get your car driving again. Use extreme caution when messing with wiring and always consult the Owner's Manual for specific instructions about the color coding and wires associated with your model. If you want to know how to get started hot-wiring the steering column and using other methods, this article will be helpful.

#Enter the car. Do not break into a car unless you own it and have documentation to prove it.  Be aware that forced entry will set an [[Shut Off a Car Alarm That Won't Quit|alarm]] if the vehicle is equipped.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 1 Version 5.jpg|center]]
#*Wires leading to the column-mounted controls on one side, like lights, [[Use Cruise Control on a Car|cruise control]], and other indicators
#*Wires leading to the column controls on the other side, like [[Change the Wiper Blades on Your Car|wipers]] or seat warmers
#*Wires leading to the [[Change a Car Battery|battery]], ignition, and starter leading straight up the steering column

#Connect the ignition on/off wire to the battery wire. You should see the dash lights and other electrical components come alive at this point. If all you want to do is listen to the radio, you're done. If you want to [[Drive a Car Safely|drive]] the car, you'll need to spark the starter wire, which can get dangerous.<ref>http://howto.wired.com/wiki/Hot_Wire_Your_Car</ref>[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 6 Version 5.jpg|center]]

#Get out your jump cables. Run a jump cable from the positive battery terminal to either the positive side of the coil, or the red wire that leads to the coil. This will give power to the [[Custom Paint a Car Dashboard|dashboard]], which is essential if you want to start the engine.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 14 Version 5.jpg|center]]
#*The locking pin will not break or set off any alarms and you should be able to find the [[Test a Starter Solenoid|solenoid]] should be underneath.

added: #Enter the car. Do not break into a car unless you own it and have documentation to prove it.  Be aware that forced entry will set an alarm if the vehicle is equipped.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 1 Version 5.jpg|center]]

#Remove the plastic cover on the steering column. These are usually held in place with concealed clips or #2 Phillips-type screws. Remove them and pull the access panels free.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 2 Version 5.jpg|center]]

#Find the wiring harness connector. Once you remove the panels on the steering column, you should see a roil of electrical wires. Don't be intimidated, learn to recognize the right bundle. There will typically be three main bundles of wires:[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 3 Version 5.jpg|center]]

#Pull aside the battery, ignition, and starter wire bundle. One of these will be the primary power supply for the ignition switch, one will be ignition wires, and the other will be the starter. The other colors will vary depending on the manufacturer. Read the owner's manual or look online to be sure you can identify all possibilities.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 4 Version 5.jpg|center]]

#Strip about {{convert|1|in|cm|adj=on|1}} of insulation from the battery wires and twist them together. Wrap them with electrician's tape if available, and do not allow them to short against metal vehicle components. Connecting these will provide electricity for the ignition components, so the engine is able to run when the starter is turned.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 5 Version 5.jpg|center]]

#Connect the ignition on/off wire to the battery wire. You should see the dash lights and other electrical components come alive at this point. If all you want to do is listen to the radio, you're done. If you want to drive the car, you'll need to spark the starter wire, which can get dangerous.<ref>http://howto.wired.com/wiki/Hot_Wire_Your_Car</ref>[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 6 Version 5.jpg|center]]

#Being extremely careful, strip the starter wire about {{convert|1/2|in|cm|adj=on|1|1}}. This will be live, so you need to extremely careful and keep close hold of your bare wires. Touch the end of this to the connected battery wires. Don't try to twist it on, just spark it against the battery wires to start the car.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 7 Version 4.jpg|center]]
#Rev the engine. If you get the car to start, rev it a few times so you don't stall out and have to do this process again.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 8 Version 5.jpg|center]]

#Break the steering lock. You've got the car started and you're ready to get your engine pumping and let your car loose, right? Wrong. While your car is running, the steering column is probably locked at this point, meaning that you'll have to break it to be able to steer, unless you want to drive straight off a cliff or something.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 9 Version 5.jpg|center]]

#Position the drill on the keyhole about 2/3 of the way up. Your goal with this method is to destroy the lock pins and allow you to turn the car over using a screwdriver, rather than the key. This is commonly done on cars the keys to which are lost.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 10 Version 5.jpg|center]]

#Drill in about the length of a key. Every lock pin has two sections followed by a spring, so drill it more than once, removing the drill each time to allow the bits of the lock inside to fall into place.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 11 Version 5.jpg|center]]

#Put the screwdriver in the same way you would put your key in. It doesn't have to go in deep because the pins are already broken. Use it the same way you use your key, just turn it about a quarter-turn in a clockwise direction to try to turn the engine over.<ref>http://www.survivalistdaily.com/how-to-hot-wire-a-car/</ref>[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 12 Version 5.jpg|center]]

#Open the hood and locate the red coil wire. Both the plug and coil wires are located at the rear of almost all V8 engines. Four-cylinder engines have them placed on the right side, near the center of the engine. Six-cylinder engines are on the opposite: left side, near the center of the engine.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 13 Version 5.jpg|center]]

#Get out your jump cables. Run a jump cable from the positive battery terminal to either the positive side of the coil, or the red wire that leads to the coil. This will give power to the dashboard, which is essential if you want to start the engine.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 14 Version 5.jpg|center]]

#Locate the starter solenoid. On Ford cars, it is on the right-side fender well, near the battery. On GM cars, it is on the starter under the steering wheel.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 15 Version 5.jpg|center]]

#Unlock the steering wheel. Place a flat blade screwdriver in the top center of the steering column, pushing between the wheel and the column. You want to push the locking pin away from the wheel. Don't worry, you're allowed to be rough here.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 16 Version 5.jpg|center]]

#Connect the solenoid to the positive battery terminal. You will see a small wire at the top of the solenoid and the positive battery cable below. Remove the ignition switch wire from the solenoid and, using an insulated screwdriver, short the solenoid’s positive post to the terminal where the ignition switch connects.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 17 Version 5.jpg|center]]

added: While most newer model cars have done much to hide the wiring and otherwise outfit the steering column with safety measures to prevent hot-wiring, older models up to the mid-90s are typically good candidates for hot-wiring. This is important to know if you lose your keys and need to get your car driving again. Use extreme caution when messing with wiring and always consult the Owner's Manual for specific instructions about the color coding and wires associated with your model. If you want to know how to get started hot-wiring the steering column and using other methods, this article will be helpful.

added: While most newer model cars have done much to hide the wiring and otherwise outfit the steering column with safety measures to prevent hot-wiring, older models up to the mid-90s are typically good candidates for hot-wiring. This is important to know if you lose your keys and need to get your car running again. Use extreme caution when messing with wiring and always consult the Owner's Manual for specific instructions about the color coding and wires associated with your model. If you want to know how to get started hot-wiring the steering column and using other methods, see Step 1 for more information.
[[Category:Car Batteries and Ignitions]]
== Steps ==
===Hot-Wiring the Steering Column===

#Enter the car. Do not break into a car unless you own it and have documentation to prove it.  Be aware that forced entry will set an alarm if the vehicle is equipped.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 1 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#*This method, and in fact most methods of hot wiring a car, will only work on cars older than the mid-90s. Newer models are equipped with a whole host of locking mechanisms in place to keep you from hot-wiring the car unless you're intimately familiar with the quirks of the model. If you try this on a 2002 Honda Civic, you're likely to end up setting off alarms and locking the starter, meaning no one can drive it.

#*If you have access to the owner's manual, check to make sure the steering column and gear selector can be overridden. Serious damage to the shifting mechanism and steering column can result from this method.

#Remove the plastic cover on the steering column. These are usually held in place with concealed clips or #2 Phillips-type screws. Remove them and pull the access panels free.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 2 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#*Alternatively, on some much older models, you can break the locking pins in the ignition by hammering a flathead screwdriver into the keyhole and turning it over. It's very difficult--if not impossible--to do this by hand, but if you think the model is sufficiently old to allow for it, you can give it a shot.

#Find the wiring harness connector. Once you remove the panels on the steering column, you should see a roil of electrical wires. Don't be intimidated, learn to recognize the right bundle. There will typically be three main bundles of wires:[[Image:407996 3.jpg|center]]
#*Wires leading to the column-mounted controls on one side, like lights, cruise control, and other indicators
#*Wires leading to the column controls on the other side, like wipers or seat warmers
#*Wires leading to the the battery, ignition, and starter leading straight up the steering column

#Pull aside the battery, ignition, and starter wire bundle. One of these will be the primary power supply for the ignition switch, one will be ignition wires, and the other will be the starter. The other colors will vary depending on the manufacturer. Read the owner's manual or look online to be sure you can identify all possibilities.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 4 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#*Sometimes the ignition wires are brown and the starter wires yellow, but the battery wires are most usually red. Again, the only way to be sure is to read the owner's manual. You're not MacGyver; messing with the wrong wires will get you electrocuted.

#Strip about {{convert|1|in|cm|adj=on|1}} of insulation from the battery wires and twist them together. Wrap them with electrician's tape if available, and do not allow them to short against metal vehicle components. Connecting these will provide electricity for the ignition components, so the engine is able to run when the starter is turned.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 5 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Connect the ignition on/off wire to the battery wire. You should see the dash lights and other electrical components come alive at this point. If all you want to do is listen to the radio, you're done. If you want to drive the car, you'll need to spark the starter wire, which can get dangerous.<ref>http://howto.wired.com/wiki/Hot_Wire_Your_Car</ref>[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 6 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Being extremely careful, strip the starter wire about {{convert|1/2|in|cm|adj=on|1|1}}. This will be live, so you need to extremely careful and keep close hold of your bare wires. Touch the end of this to the connected battery wires. Don't try to twist it on, just spark it against the battery wires to start the car.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 7 Version 2.jpg|center]]
#Rev the engine. If you get the car to start, rev it a few times so you don't stall out and have to do this process again.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 8 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#*Once the engine starts, you can remove the starter wire and continue on your way. When you want to kill the engine, simply unfasten the battery wires from the ignition wires and the car will die.<ref>http://jalopnik.com/5871510/how-to-hotwire-a-car/gallery/?comment=45569978#comments</ref>

#Break the steering lock. You've got the car started and you're ready to tear off into the sunset, right? Wrong. While your car is running, the steering column is probably locked at this point, meaning that you'll have to break it to be able to steer, unless you want to drive straight off a cliff or something.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 9 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#*On some models, all you'll need to do is pop off the metal keyhole which will release a spring and break the lock. If you already tried to jam your screwdriver in there earlier because you've got a mid-70s to mid-80s vehicle, the lock is probably already broken.

#*Some models respond well to a healthy dose of elbow grease. Crank the wheel hard to either side as if you were trying to twist it free. You could also use a hammer to fix in the wheel and use for leverage. You should hear it break and the wheel will be free, so you'll be able to drive normally.
===Drilling the Lock Pins===

#Position the drill on the keyhole about 2/3 of the way up. Your goal with this method is to destroy the lock pins and allow you to turn the car over using a screwdriver, rather than the key. This is commonly done on cars the keys to which are lost.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 10 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Drill in about the length of a key. Every lock pin has two sections followed by a spring, so drill it more than once, removing the drill each time to allow the bits of the lock inside to fall into place.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 11 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Put the screwdriver in the same way you would put your key in. It doesn't have to go in deep because the pins are already broken. Use it the same way you use your key, just turn it about a quarter-turn in a clockwise direction to try to turn the engine over.<ref>http://www.survivalistdaily.com/how-to-hot-wire-a-car/</ref>[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 12 Version 3.jpg|center]]
#*Warning: this method will destroy your key switch and make it so that anyone with a screwdriver or a strong fingernail can steal your car.
===Powering the Dash===

#Open the hood and locate the red coil wire. Both the plug and coil wires are located at the rear of almost all V8 engines. Four-cylinder engines have them placed on the right side, near the center of the engine. Six-cylinder engines are on the opposite: left side, near the center of the engine.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 13 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Get out your jump cables. Run a jump cable from the positive battery terminal to either the positive side of the coil, or the red wire that leads to the coil. This will give power to the dashboard, which is essential if you want to start the engine.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 14 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Locate the starter solenoid. On Ford cars, it is on the right-side fender well, near the battery. On GM cars, it is on the starter under the steering wheel.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 15 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Unlock the steering wheel. Place a flat blade screwdriver in the top center of the steering column, pushing between the wheel and the column. You want to push the locking pin away from the wheel. Don't worry, you're allowed to be rough here.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 16 Version 3.jpg|center]]
#*The locking pin will not break or set off any alarms and you should be able to find the solenoid should be underneath.

#Connect the solenoid to the positive battery terminal. You will see a small wire at the top of the solenoid and the positive battery cable below. Remove the ignition switch wire from the solenoid and, using an insulated screwdriver, short the solenoid’s positive post to the terminal where the ignition switch connects.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 17 Version 3.jpg|center]]
#*Doing so will apply 12 volts directly from the battery. This should activate the solenoid, and the starter should crank the car.
== Video ==
{{Video:Hotwire a Car|}}
== Tips ==
*You risk causing significant damage to your vehicle if you hotwire it.
*Vehicles with a computer chip in the ignition switch cannot be hot wired, the chip enables the Electronic Control Module to function, and without it, the car will not run.
*Never leave the ignition wires twisted together when you finish running the engine.  This can burn up the ignition system of the vehicle, and will at least discharge the battery.
* Most cars set off an alarm if you hot-wire it wrong.
*Use this knowledge responsibly.
== Warnings ==
*Wear insulated gloves.
*If the ignition wires separate while driving, the engine will instantly die, and you may find yourself without power, steering, or brakes.
*'''Don't''' use this in an illegal manner, such as to steal a car.

*You risk causing significant damage to your vehicle if you hotwire it.
*Vehicles with a computer chip in the ignition switch cannot be hot wired, the chip enables the Electronic Control Module to function, and without it, the car will not run.
*Never leave the ignition wires twisted together when you finish running the engine.  This can burn up the ignition system of the vehicle, and will at least discharge the battery.
* Most cars set off an alarm if you hot-wire it wrong.
*Use this knowledge responsibly.
== Warnings ==
*Wear insulated gloves.
*If the ignition wires separate while driving, the engine will instantly die, and you may find yourself without power, steering, or brakes.
*'''Don't''' use this in an illegal manner, such as to steal a car.

added: #Enter the car. Do not break into a car unless you own it and have documentation to prove it.  Be aware that forced entry will set an alarm if the vehicle is equipped.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 1 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Remove the plastic cover on the steering column. These are usually held in place with concealed clips or #2 Phillips-type screws. Remove them and pull the access panels free.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 2 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Find the wiring harness connector. Once you remove the panels on the steering column, you should see a roil of electrical wires. Don't be intimidated, learn to recognize the right bundle. There will typically be three main bundles of wires:[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 3 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Pull aside the battery, ignition, and starter wire bundle. One of these will be the primary power supply for the ignition switch, one will be ignition wires, and the other will be the starter. The other colors will vary depending on the manufacturer. Read the owner's manual or look online to be sure you can identify all possibilities.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 4 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Strip about {{convert|1|in|cm|adj=on|1}} of insulation from the battery wires and twist them together. Wrap them with electrician's tape if available, and do not allow them to short against metal vehicle components. Connecting these will provide electricity for the ignition components, so the engine is able to run when the starter is turned.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 5 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Connect the ignition on/off wire to the battery wire. You should see the dash lights and other electrical components come alive at this point. If all you want to do is listen to the radio, you're done. If you want to drive the car, you'll need to spark the starter wire, which can get dangerous.<ref>http://howto.wired.com/wiki/Hot_Wire_Your_Car</ref>[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 6 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Being extremely careful, strip the starter wire about {{convert|1/2|in|cm|adj=on|1|1}}. This will be live, so you need to extremely careful and keep close hold of your bare wires. Touch the end of this to the connected battery wires. Don't try to twist it on, just spark it against the battery wires to start the car.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 7 Version 2.jpg|center]]
#Rev the engine. If you get the car to start, rev it a few times so you don't stall out and have to do this process again.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 8 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Break the steering lock. You've got the car started and you're ready to tear off into the sunset, right? Wrong. While your car is running, the steering column is probably locked at this point, meaning that you'll have to break it to be able to steer, unless you want to drive straight off a cliff or something.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 9 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Position the drill on the keyhole about 2/3 of the way up. Your goal with this method is to destroy the lock pins and allow you to turn the car over using a screwdriver, rather than the key. This is commonly done on cars the keys to which are lost.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 10 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Drill in about the length of a key. Every lock pin has two sections followed by a spring, so drill it more than once, removing the drill each time to allow the bits of the lock inside to fall into place.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 11 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Put the screwdriver in the same way you would put your key in. It doesn't have to go in deep because the pins are already broken. Use it the same way you use your key, just turn it about a quarter-turn in a clockwise direction to try to turn the engine over.<ref>http://www.survivalistdaily.com/how-to-hot-wire-a-car/</ref>[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 12 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Open the hood and locate the red coil wire. Both the plug and coil wires are located at the rear of almost all V8 engines. Four-cylinder engines have them placed on the right side, near the center of the engine. Six-cylinder engines are on the opposite: left side, near the center of the engine.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 13 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Get out your jump cables. Run a jump cable from the positive battery terminal to either the positive side of the coil, or the red wire that leads to the coil. This will give power to the dashboard, which is essential if you want to start the engine.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 14 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Locate the starter solenoid. On Ford cars, it is on the right-side fender well, near the battery. On GM cars, it is on the starter under the steering wheel.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 15 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Unlock the steering wheel. Place a flat blade screwdriver in the top center of the steering column, pushing between the wheel and the column. You want to push the locking pin away from the wheel. Don't worry, you're allowed to be rough here.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 16 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Connect the solenoid to the positive battery terminal. You will see a small wire at the top of the solenoid and the positive battery cable below. Remove the ignition switch wire from the solenoid and, using an insulated screwdriver, short the solenoid’s positive post to the terminal where the ignition switch connects.[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 17 Version 3.jpg|center]]

added: While most newer model cars have done much to hide the wiring and otherwise outfit the steering column with safety measures to prevent hot-wiring, older models up to the mid-90s are typically good candidates for hot-wiring. This is important to know if you lose your keys and need to get your car running again. Use extreme caution when messing with wiring and always consult the Owner's Manual for specific instructions about the color coding and wires associated with your model. If you want to know how to get started hot-wiring the steering column and using other methods, see Step 1 for more information.
[[Category:Car Batteries and Ignitions]]
== Steps ==
===Hot-Wiring the Steering Column===

#Enter the car. Do not break into a car unless you own it and have documentation to prove it.  Be aware that forced entry will set an alarm if the vehicle is equipped.{{largeimage|Hotwire a Car Step 9.jpg}}

#*This method, and in fact most methods of hotwiring a car, will only work on cars older than the mid-90s. Newer models are equipped with a whole host of locking mechanisms in place to keep you from hotwiring the car unless you're intimately familiar with the quirks of the model. If you try this on a 2002 Honda Civic, you're likely to end up setting off alarms and locking the starter, meaning no one can drive it.

#*If you have access to the owner's manual, check to make sure the steering column and gear selector can be overridden. Serious damage to the shifting mechanism and steering column can result from this method.

#Remove the plastic cover on the steering column. These are usually held in place with concealed clips or #2 Phillips-type screws. Remove them and pull the access panels free.{{largeimage|Hotwire a Car Step 11.jpg}}

#*Alternatively, on some much older models, you can break the locking pins in the ignition by hammering a flathead screwdriver into the keyhole and turning it over. It's very difficult--if not impossible--to do this by hand, but if you think the model is sufficiently old to allow for it, you can give it a shot.

#Find the wiring harness connector. Once you remove the panels on the steering column, you should see a roil of electrical wires. Don't be intimidated, learn to recognize the right bundle. There will typically be three main bundles of wires:{{largeimage|Hotwire a Car Step 12.jpg}}
#*Wires leading to the column-mounted controls on one side, like lights, cruise control, and other indicators
#*Wires leading to the column controls on the other side, like wipers or seat warmers
#*Wires leading to the the battery, ignition, and starter leading straight up the steering column

#Pull aside the battery, ignition, and starter wire bundle. One of these will be the primary power supply for the ignition switch, one will be ignition wires, and the other will be the starter. The other colors will vary depending on the manufacturer. Read the owner's manual or look online to be sure you can identify all possibilities. {{largeimage|Hotwire a Car Step 13.jpg}}

#*Sometimes the ignition wires are brown and the starter wires yellow, but the battery wires are most usually red. Again, the only way to be sure is to read the owner's manual. You're not MacGuyver; messing with the wrong wires will get you electrocuted.

#Strip about 1 inch of insulation from the battery wires and twist them together. Wrap them with electrician's tape if available, and do not allow them to short against metal vehicle components. Connecting these will provide electricity for the ignition components, so the engine is able to run when the starter is turned.

#Connect the ignition on/off wire to the battery wire. You should see the dash lights and other electrical components come alive at this point. If all you want to do is listen to the radio, you're done. If you want to drive the car, you'll need to spark the starter wire, which can get dangerous.<ref>http://howto.wired.com/wiki/Hot_Wire_Your_Car</ref>

#Being extremely careful, strip the starter wire about 1/2 inch. This will be live, so you need to extremely careful and keep close hold of your bare wires. Touch the end of this to the connected battery wires. Don't try and twist it on, just spark it agains the battery wires to start the car.{{largeimage|Hotwire a Car Step 15.jpg}}
#Rev the engine. If you get the car to start, rev it a few times so you don't stall out and have to do this process again.{{largeimage|Hotwire a Car Step 17.jpg}}

#*Once the engine starts, you can remove the starter wire and continue on your way. When you want to kill the engine, simply unfasten the battery wires from the ignition wires and the car will die.<ref>http://jalopnik.com/5871510/how-to-hotwire-a-car/gallery/?comment=45569978#comments</ref>

#Break the steering lock. You've got the car started and you're ready to tear off into the sunset, right? Wrong. While your car is running, the steering column is probably locked at this point, meaning that you'll have to break it to be able to steer, unless you want to drive straight off a cliff or something.

#*On some models, all you'll need to do is pop off the metal key hole which will release a spring and break the lock. If you already tried to jam your screwdriver in there earlier because you've got a mid-70s to mid-80s vehicle, the lock is probably already broken.

#*Some models respond well to a healthy dose of elbow grease. Crank the wheel hard to either side as if you were trying to twist it free. You could also use a hammer to fix in the wheel and use for leverage. You should hear it break and the wheel will be free, so you'll be able to drive normally.
===Drilling the Lock Pins===

#Position the drill on the keyhole about 2/3 of the way up. Your goal with this method is to destroy the lock pins and allow you to turn the car over using a screwdriver, rather than the key. This is commonly done on cars the keys to which are lost.

#Drill in about the length of a key. Every lock pin has two sections followed by a spring, so drill it more than once, removing the drill each time to allow the bits of the lock inside to fall into place.

# Put the screwdriver in the same way you would put your key in. It doesn't have to go in deep because the pins are already broken. Use it the same way you use your key, just turn it about a quarter-turn in a clockwise direction to try and turn the engine over.<ref>http://www.survivalistdaily.com/how-to-hot-wire-a-car/</ref>
#*Warning: this method will destroy your key switch and make it so that anyone with a screwdriver or a strong fingernail can steal your car.
===Powering the Dash===

#Open the hood and locate the red coil wire. Both the plug and coil wires are located at the rear of almost all V8 engines. Four-cylinder engines have them placed on the right side, near the center of the engine. Six-cylinder engines are on the opposite: left side, near the center of the engine.{{largeimage|Hotwire a Car Step 2.jpg}}

#Get out your jump cables. Run a jump cable from the positive battery terminal to either the positive side of the coil, or the red wire that leads to the coil. This will give power to the dashboard, which is essential if you want to start the engine.{{largeimage|Hotwire a Car Step 4.jpg}}
#Locate the starter solenoid. On Ford cars, it is on the right-side fender well, near the battery. On GM cars, it is on the starter under the steering wheel.{{largeimage|Hotwire a Car Step 5.jpg}}

#Unlock the steering wheel. Place a flat blade screwdriver in the top center of the steering column, pushing between the wheel and the column. You want to push the locking pin away from the wheel. Don't worry, you're allowed to be rough here.{{largeimage|Hotwire a Car Step 7.jpg}}
#*The locking pin will not break or set off any alarms and you should be able to find the solenoid should be underneath.

#Connect the solenoid to the positive battery terminal. You will see a small wire at the top of the solenoid and the positive battery cable below. Remove the ignition switch wire from the solenoid and, using an insulated screwdriver, short the solenoid’s positive post to the terminal where the ignition switch connects. {{largeimage|Hotwire a Car Step 8.jpg}}
#*Doing so will apply 12 volts directly from the battery. This should activate the solenoid, and the starter should crank the car.
== Video ==
{{Video:Hotwire a Car|}}
== Tips ==
*You risk causing significant damage to your vehicle if you hotwire it.
*Never leave the ignition wires twisted together when you finish running the engine.  This can burn up the ignition system of the vehicle, and will at least discharge the battery.
* Most cars set off an alarm if you hot-wire it wrong.
*Use this knowledge responsibly.
*Vehicles with a computer chip in the ignition switch cannot be hot wired, the chip enables the Electronic Control Module to function, and without it, the car will not run.
== Warnings ==
*If the ignition wires separate while driving, the engine will instantly die, and you may find yourself without power, steering, or brakes.
*Wear insulated gloves.
*'''Don't''' use this in an illegal manner, such as to steal a car.

# Enter the car. Do not break into a car unless you own it and have documentation to prove it.  Be aware that forced entry will set an alarm if the vehicle is equipped.{{largeimage|Hotwire a Car Step 9.jpg}}

# Determine if the steering column and gear selector can be overridden, if so equipped.  Serious damage to the shifting mechanism and/or steering column will result in forcing these theft deterrent mechanisms in an attempt to override them.{{largeimage|Hotwire a Car Step 10.jpg}}

Every pin has 2 sections, followed by a spring, so drill it more than once, removing the drill each time to allow the bits of the lock inside to fall into place.

There is a huge risk of electrical shock while hot-wiring, and it may not work in many cases. Some newer model cars have the required components hidden so you can't reach them. Others have "kill switches", which shut down the engine so that it cannot be started, even with the key. Older model cars, as well as some hybrid and electric cars, will work.
[[Category:Car Batteries and Ignitions]]
== Steps ==
===Method 1===

#Open the hood.

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 1.jpg|center|500px]]

#Locate the red coil wire. Both the plug and coil wires are located at the rear (back) of almost all V8 engines. Four-cylinder engines have them placed on the right side, near the center of the engine.  Six-cylinder engines are on the opposite: left side, near the center of the engine .

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 2.jpg|center|500px]]

#Locate the battery (it's square and has two red and black cables).

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 3.jpg|center|500px]]

#Run a wire from the positive side of the battery (not negative!) to either the positive side of the coil, or the red wire that leads to the coil. This will give power to the dashboard, which is essential if you ever want it to start.

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 4.jpg|center|500px]]

#Locate the starter solenoid. On Ford cars, it is on the right-side fender well, near the battery. On GM cars, it is on the starter under the steering wheel.

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 5.jpg|center|500px]]

#If under the steering wheel, enter the car without setting off any alarms. If it has standard transmission, make sure the car is in neutral and the parking brake is on.

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 6.jpg|center|500px]]

#Unlock the steering wheel by taking a flat blade screwdriver and placing it at the top center of the steering column. Push the screwdriver between the wheel and the column, then push the locking pin away from the wheel. Don't worry, you're allowed to be rough here. The locking pin will not break or set off any alarms. The solenoid should be underneath.

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 7.jpg|center|500px]]

#  You will see a small wire at the top of the solenoid and the positive battery cable below. Cross the two different terminal that they are connected to with a screwdriver or pliers. This will crank the engine, giving you leave to drive. Congratulations.

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 8.jpg|center|500px]]
===Method 2===

# Enter the car. Do not break into a car unless you own it and have documentation to prove it.  Be aware that forced entry will set an alarm if the vehicle is equipped.

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 9.jpg|center|500px]]

# Determine if the steering column and gear selector can be overridden, if so equipped.  Serious damage to the shifting mechanism and/or steering column will result in forcing these theft deterrent mechanisms in an attempt to override them.

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 10.jpg|center|500px]]

# Look under steering wheel.  This may require taking an access cover off.  These are usually held in place with concealed clips or #2 Phillips type screws.  Remove if needed.

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 11.jpg|center|500px]]

# See if there is a clip or wiring harness connector in which you can gain access to the wires behind the ignition.

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 12.jpg|center|500px]]

# Look for the two wires that are the same, usually red and strip them and twist them together.  One of these will be the primary power supply for the ignition switch, the other will be the connection for the vehicle's electrical circuits that are energised when the key is turn to the run position.  Connecting these will provide electricity for the ignition components, so the engine is able to run when the starter is turned.

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 13.jpg|center|500px]]

# Strip about 1 inch of insulation from this pair of wires, and twist them tightly together.  Wrap with electrician's tape if available, and do not allow them to short against metal vehicle components.

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 14.jpg|center|500px]]

# Get the ignition wire, brown in many cars, strip it about 1/2 inch, and touch the end of the stripped brown wire with the connected red wires.

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 15.jpg|center|500px]]

# Do not twist the brown wire to the reds, just touch the wires until ignition has been achieved.

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 16.jpg|center|500px]]

# Rev the engine enough so you don't stall and have to do this process again.

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 17.jpg|center|500px]]
===Method 3===

#This is the most effective method due to the fact that you don't need to bother keeping wires together, raising the hood, or unlocking the steering wheel.  If you hotwire it with the wires only, your steering wheel WILL NOT TURN unless you break the steering lock. The "classic screwdriver method" where you put a screwdriver in the lock and twist doesn't work because you can't generate enough torque with your bare hands to make the lock pins break off without breaking the lock off of its mounting structure, thereby rendering the car useless. Use this method instead.
# Gather materials: 1 flathead screwdriver with an insulated handle, 1 cordless drill and a small drill bit.

# Take it from an expert:  So, there is a flap at the end of the keyhole.  Position the drill on the keyhole about 2/3 of the way up and drill in about the length of a key.  This will destroy your lock pins and make the key switch able to be turned on and off without a key. Every pin has 2 sections, followed by a spring, so drill it more than once, removing the drill each time to allow the bits of the lock inside to fall into place.
# Put the screwdriver in the same way you would put your key in, it doesn't have to go in deep because the pins are already broken.
# Use it the same way you use your key, just turn it.
#*Warning: this method will destroy your key switch and make it so that anyone with a screwdriver or a strong fingernail can steal your car.
== Video ==
{{Video:Hotwire a Car|}}
Video on Youtube:
Search, How to Hotwire a Car, First Video.
== Tips ==
*Use this knowledge responsibly.
*Vehicles with a computer chip in the ignition switch cannot be hot wired, the chip enables the ECM to function, and without it, the car will not run.
*You risk causing significant damage to your vehicle if you hotwire it.
*Never leave the ignition wires twisted together when you finish running the engine.  This can burn up the ignition system of the vehicle, and will at least discharge the battery.
== Warnings ==
*Wear insulated gloves.
*If the ignition wires separate while driving, the engine will instantly die, and you may find yourself without power, steering, or brakes.
*'''Don't''' use this in an illegal manner, such as to steal a car.

added:
#Open the hood.

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 1.jpg|center|500px]]

#Locate the red coil wire. Both the plug and coil wires are located at the rear (back) of almost all V-8 engines. Four-cylinder engines have them placed on the right side, near the center of the engine.  Six-cylinder engines are on the opposite: left side, near the center of the engine .

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 2.jpg|center|500px]]

#Locate the battery (it's square and has two red and black cables).

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 3.jpg|center|500px]]

#Run a wire from the positive side of the battery (not negative!) to either the positive side of the coil, or the red wire that leads to the coil. This will give power to the dashboard, which is essential if you ever want it to start.

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 4.jpg|center|500px]]

#Locate the starter solenoid. On Fords, it is on the passenger-side fender well, near the battery. On GMs, it is on the starter under the steering wheel.

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 5.jpg|center|500px]]

#If under the steering wheel, enter the car without setting off any alarms. If it has standard transmission, make sure the car is in neutral and the parking brake is on.

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 6.jpg|center|500px]]

#Unlock the steering wheel by taking a flat blade screwdriver and placing it at the top center of the steering column. Push the screwdriver between the wheel and the column, then push the locking pin away from the wheel. Don't worry, you're allowed to be rough here. The locking pin will not break or set off any alarms. The solenoid should be underneath.

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 7.jpg|center|500px]]

#  You will see a small wire at the top of the solenoid and the positive battery cable below. Cross the two different terminal that they are connected to with a screwdriver or pliers. This will crank the engine, giving you leave to drive. Congratulations.

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 8.jpg|center|500px]]

# Enter car.  Do not break into a car unless you own it and have documentation to prove it.  Be aware that forced entry will set an intrusion alarm off if the vehicle is so equipped.

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 9.jpg|center|500px]]

# Determine if the steering column and gear selector can be overridden, if so equipped.  Serious damage to the shifting mechanism and/or steering column will result in forcing these theft deterrant mechanisms in an attempt to override them.

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 10.jpg|center|500px]]

# Look under steering wheel.  This may require taking an access cover off.  These are usually held in place with concealed clips or #2 Phillips type screws.  Remove if needed.

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 11.jpg|center|500px]]

# See if there is a clip or wiring harness connector in which you can gain access to the wires behind the ignition.

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 12.jpg|center|500px]]

# Look for the two wires that are the same, usually red and strip them and twist them together.  One of these will be the primary power supply for the ignition switch, the other will be the connection for the vehicle's electrical circuits that are energised when the key is turn to the run position.  Connecting these will provide electricity for the ignition components, so the engine is able to run when the starter is turned.

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 13.jpg|center|500px]]

# Strip about 1 inch of insulation from this pair of wires, and twist them tightly together.  Wrap with electrician's tape if available, and do not allow them to short against metal vehicle components.

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 14.jpg|center|500px]]

# Get the ignition wire, brown in many cars, strip it about 1/2 inch, and touch the end of the stripped brown wire with the connected red wires.

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 15.jpg|center|500px]]

# Do not twist the brown wire to the reds, just touch the wires until ignition has been achieved.

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 16.jpg|center|500px]]

# Rev the engine enough so you don't stall and have to do this process again.

[[Image:Hotwire a Car Step 17.jpg|center|500px]]

added: [[Image:M52TUB25 4108.jpg|thumb|A BMW standard engine. Not the most fun to try this on.]]This is a step by step guide to hotwiring a car. Hot-wiring is absolutely illegal without the owner's permission, unless the car is being repossessed (in which case the "owner" no longer owns the car anyway). There is a huge risk of electrical shock while hot-wiring, and it may not work in many cases. Some newer model cars have the required components hidden so you can't reach them. Others have "kill switches," which shut down the engine so that it cannot be started, even with the key. Older model cars, like any gas-guzzler from 2004 on down, will work.  So will some hybrid and electric cars.
[[Category:Car Maintenance and Repair]]
[[Category:Electronics]]
== Steps ==
===Method 1===
#Open the hood.

#Locate the red coil wire. Both the plug and coil wires are located at the rear(back) of almost all V-8 engines. Four-cylinder engines have them placed on the right side, near the center of the engine.  Six-cylinder engines are on the opposite: left side, near the center of the engine .
#Locate the battery (it's square and has two red and black cables).

#Run a wire from the positive side of the battery (not negative!) to either the positive side of the coil, or the red wire that leads to the coil. This will give power to the dashboard, which is essential if you ever want it to start.
#Locate the starter solenoid. On Fords, it is on the passenger-side fender well, near the battery. On GMs, it is on the starter under the steering wheel.
#If under the steering wheel, enter the car without setting off any alarms. If it has standard transmission, make sure the car is in neutral and the parking brake is on.

#Unlock the steering wheel by taking a flat blade screwdriver and placing it at the top center of the steering column. Push the screwdriver between the wheel and the column, then push the locking pin away from the wheel. Don't worry, you're allowed to be rough here. The locking pin will not break or set off any alarms. The solenoid should be underneath.

#  You will see a small wire at the top of the solenoid and the positive battery cable below. Cross the two different terminal that they are connected to with a screwdriver or pliers. This will crank the engine, giving you leave to drive. Congratulations.
===Method 2===
# Enter car.  Do not break into a car unless you own it and have documentation to prove it.  Be aware that forced entry will set an intrusion alarm off if the vehicle is so equipped.

# Determine if the steering column and gear selector can be overridden, if so equipped.  Serious damage to the shifting mechanism and/or steering column will result in forcing these theft deterrant mechanisms in an attempt to override them.
# Look under steering wheel.  This may require taking an access cover off.  These are usually held in place with concealed clips or #2 Phillips type screws.  Remove if needed.
# See if there is a clip or wiring harness connector in which you can gain access to the wires behind the ignition.

# Look for the two wires that are the same, usually red and strip them and twist them together.  One of these will be the primary power supply for the ignition switch, the other will be the connection for the vehicle's electrical circuits that are energised when the key is turn to the run position.  Connecting these will provide electricity for the ignition components, so the engine is able to run when the starter is turned.

# Strip about 1 inch of insulation from this pair of wires, and twist them tightly together.  Wrap with electrician's tape if available, and do not allow them to short against metal vehicle components.
# Get the ignition wire, brown in many cars, strip it about 1/2 inch, and touch the end of the stripped brown wire with the connected red wires.
# Do not twist the brown wire to the reds, just touch the wires until ignition has been achieved.
# Rev the engine enough so you don't stall and have to do this process again.
===Method 3===

This is the most effective method due to the fact that you don't need to bother keeping wires together, raising the hood, or unlocking the steering wheel.  If you hotwire it with the wires only, your steering wheel WILL NOT TURN unless you break the steering lock. The "classic screwdriver method" where you put a screwdriver in the lock and twist doesn't work because you can't generate enough torque with your bare hands to make the lock pins break off without breaking the lock off of its mounting structure, thereby rendering the car useless. Use this method instead.
# Gather materials: 1 flathead screwdriver with an insulated handle, 1 cordless drill and a small drill bit.

# Take it from an expert:  So, there is a flap at the end of the keyhole.  Position the drill on the keyhole about 2/3 of the way up and drill in about the length of a key.  This will destroy your lock pins and make the key switch able to be turned on and off without a key. Every pin has 2 sections, followed by a spring, so drill it more than once, removing the drill each time to allow the bits of the lock inside to fall into place.
# Put the screwdriver in the same way you would put your key in, it doesn't have to go in deep because the pins are already broken.
# Use it the same way you use your key, just turn it.
#*Warning: this method will destroy your key switch and make it so anyone with a screwdriver or an exceptionally strong fingernail to steal your car.
== Video ==
{{Video:Hotwire a Car|}}
Video on Youtube:
Search, How to Hotwire a Car, First Video.
== Tips ==
*Use this knowledge responsibly.
*Vehicles with a computer chip in the ignition switch cannot be hot wired, the chip enables the ECM to function, and without it, the car will not run.
*You risk causing significant damage to your vehicle if you hotwire it.
*Never leave the ignition wires twisted together when you finish running the engine.  This can burn up the ignition system of the vehicle, and will at least discharge the battery.
== Warnings ==
*Wear insulated gloves.
*If the ignition wires separate while driving, the engine will instantly die, and you may find yourself without power, steering, or brakes.
*'''Don't''' use this in an illegal manner, such as to steal a car.  Chances are you'll be caught, and prison is not a fun place..
{{dangerous}}

added: {{nfd|dup|Hot Wire a Car|date=2010-07-11}}[[Image:M52TUB25 4108.jpg|thumb|A BMW standard engine. Not the most fun to try this on.]]This is a step by step guide to hotwiring a car. Hot-wiring is absolutely illegal without the owner's permission, unless the car is being repossessed (in which case the "owner" no longer owns the car anyway). There is a huge risk of electrical shock while hot-wiring, and it may not work in many cases. Some newer model cars have the required components hidden so you can't reach them. Others have "kill switches," which shut down the engine so that it cannot be started, even with the key. Older model cars, like any gas-guzzler from 2004 on down, will work.  So will some hybrid and electric cars.
[[Category:Detect and Fix Problems]]
[[Category:Car Maintenance and Repair]]
[[Category:Electronics]]
== Steps ==
===Method 1===
# Open the hood.

#  Locate the red coil wire. Both the plug and coil wires are located at the rear(back) of almost all V-8 engines. Four-cylinder engines have them placed on the right side, near the center of the engine.  Six-cylinder engines are on the opposite: left side, near the center of the engine .
#  Locate the battery (it's square and has two red and black cables).

#  Run a wire from the positive side of the battery (not negative!) to either the positive side of the coil, or the red wire that leads to the coil. This will give power to the dashboard, which is essential if you ever want it to start.
#  Locate the starter solenoid. On Fords, it is on the passenger-side fender well, near the battery. On GMs, it is on the starter under the steering wheel.
#  If under the steering wheel, enter the car without setting off any alarms. If it has standard transmission, make sure the car is in neutral and the parking brake is on.

#  Unlock the steering wheel by taking a flat blade screwdriver and placing it at the top center of the steering column. Push the screwdriver between the wheel and the column, then push the locking pin away from the wheel. Don't worry, you're allowed to be rough here. The locking pin will not break or set off any alarms. The solenoid should be underneath.

#  You will see a small wire at the top of the solenoid and the positive battery cable below. Cross the two different terminal that they are connected to with a screwdriver or pliers. This will crank the engine, giving you leave to drive. Congratulations.
===Method 2===
# Enter car.  Do not break into a car unless you own it and have documentation to prove it.  Be aware that forced entry will set an intrusion alarm off if the vehicle is so equipped.

# Determine if the steering column and gear selector can be overridden, if so equipped.  Serious damage to the shifting mechanism and/or steering column will result in forcing these theft deterrant mechanisms in an attempt to override them.
# Look under steering wheel.  This may require taking an access cover off.  These are usually held in place with concealed clips or #2 Phillips type screws.  Remove if needed.
# See if there is a clip or wiring harness connector in which you can gain access to the wires behind the ignition.

# Look for the two wires that are the same, usually red and strip them and twist them together.  One of these will be the primary power supply for the ignition switch, the other will be the connection for the vehicle's electrical circuits that are energised when the key is turn to the run position.  Connecting these will provide electricity for the ignition components, so the engine is able to run when the starter is turned.

# Strip about 1 inch of insulation from this pair of wires, and twist them tightly together.  Wrap with electrician's tape if available, and do not allow them to short against metal vehicle components.
# Get the ignition wire, brown in many cars, strip it about 1/2 inch, and touch the end of the stripped brown wire with the connected red wires.
# Do not twist the brown wire to the reds, just touch the wires until ignition has been achieved.
# Rev the engine enough so you don't stall and have to do this process again.
===Method 3===

This is the most effective method due to the fact that you don't need to bother keeping wires together, raising the hood, or unlocking the steering wheel.  If you hotwire it with the wires only, your steering wheel WILL NOT TURN unless you break the steering lock. The "classic screwdriver method" where you put a screwdriver in the lock and twist doesn't work because you can't generate enough torque with your bare hands to make the lock pins break off without breaking the lock off of its mounting structure, thereby rendering the car useless. Use this method instead.
# Gather materials: 1 flathead screwdriver with an insulated handle, 1 cordless drill and a small drill bit.

# Take it from an expert:  So, there is a flap at the end of the keyhole.  Position the drill on the keyhole about 2/3 of the way up and drill in about the length of a key.  This will destroy your lock pins and make the key switch able to be turned on and off without a key. Every pin has 2 sections, followed by a spring, so drill it more than once, removing the drill each time to allow the bits of the lock inside to fall into place.
# Put the screwdriver in the same way you would put your key in, it doesn't have to go in deep because the pins are already broken.
# Use it the same way you use your key, just turn it.
#*Warning: this method will destroy your key switch and make it so anyone with a screwdriver or an exceptionally strong fingernail to steal your car.
== Video ==
{{Video:Hotwire a Car|}}
Video on Youtube:
Search, How to Hotwire a Car, First Video.
== Tips ==
*Use this knowledge responsibly.
*Vehicles with a computer chip in the ignition switch cannot be hot wired, the chip enables the ECM to function, and without it, the car will not run.
*You risk causing significant damage to your vehicle if you hotwire it.
*Never leave the ignition wires twisted together when you finish running the engine.  This can burn up the ignition system of the vehicle, and will at least discharge the battery.
== Warnings ==
*Wear insulated gloves.
*If the ignition wires separate while driving, the engine will instantly die, and you may find yourself without power, steering, or brakes.
*'''Don't''' use this in an illegal manner, such as to steal a car.  Chances are you'll be caught, and prison is not a fun place..
{{dangerous}}

added: == Steps ==
===Method 1===
# Open the hood.

#  Locate the red coil wire. Both the plug and coil wires are located at the rear(back) of almost all V-8 engines. Four-cylinder engines have them placed on the right side, near the center of the engine.  Six-cylinder engines are on the opposite: left side, near the center of the engine .
#  Locate the battery (it's square and has two red and black cables).

#  Run a wire from the positive side of the battery (not negative!) to either the positive side of the coil, or the red wire that leads to the coil. This will give power to the dashboard, which is essential if you ever want it to start.
#  Locate the starter solenoid. On Fords, it is on the passenger-side fender well, near the battery. On GMs, it is on the starter under the steering wheel.
#  If under the steering wheel, enter the car without setting off any alarms. If it has standard transmission, make sure the car is in neutral and the parking brake is on.

#  Unlock the steering wheel by taking a flat blade screwdriver and placing it at the top center of the steering column. Push the screwdriver between the wheel and the column, then push the locking pin away from the wheel. Don't worry, you're allowed to be rough here. The locking pin will not break or set off any alarms. The solenoid should be underneath.

#  You will see a small wire at the top of the solenoid and the positive battery cable below. Cross the two different terminal that they are connected to with a screwdriver or pliers. This will crank the engine, giving you leave to drive. Congratulations.
===Method 2===
# Enter car.  Do not break into a car unless you own it and have documentation to prove it.  Be aware that forced entry will set an intrusion alarm off if the vehicle is so equipped.

# Determine if the steering column and gear selector can be overridden, if so equipped.  Serious damage to the shifting mechanism and/or steering column will result in forcing these theft deterrant mechanisms in an attempt to override them.
# Look under steering wheel.  This may require taking an access cover off.  These are usually held in place with concealed clips or #2 Phillips type screws.  Remove if needed.
# See if there is a clip or wiring harness connector in which you can gain access to the wires behind the ignition.

# Look for the two wires that are the same, usually red and strip them and twist them together.  One of these will be the primary power supply for the ignition switch, the other will be the connection for the vehicle's electrical circuits that are energised when the key is turn to the run position.  Connecting these will provide electricity for the ignition components, so the engine is able to run when the starter is turned.

# Strip about 1 inch of insulation from this pair of wires, and twist them tightly together.  Wrap with electrician's tape if available, and do not allow them to short against metal vehicle components.
# Get the ignition wire, brown in many cars, strip it about 1/2 inch, and touch the end of the stripped brown wire with the connected red wires.
# Do not twist the brown wire to the reds, just touch the wires until ignition has been achieved.
# Rev the engine enough so you don't stall and have to do this process again.
===Method 3===

This is the most effective method due to the fact that you don't need to bother keeping wires together, raising the hood, or unlocking the steering wheel.  If you hotwire it with the wires only, your steering wheel WILL NOT TURN unless you break the steering lock. The "classic screwdriver method" where you put a screwdriver in the lock and twist doesn't work because you can't generate enough torque with your bare hands to make the lock pins break off without breaking the lock off of its mounting structure, thereby rendering the car useless. Use this method instead.
# Gather materials: 1 flathead screwdriver with an insulated handle, 1 cordless drill and a small drill bit.

# Take it from an expert:  So, there is a flap at the end of the keyhole.  Position the drill on the keyhole about 2/3 of the way up and drill in about the length of a key.  This will destroy your lock pins and make the key switch able to be turned on and off without a key. Every pin has 2 sections, followed by a spring, so drill it more than once, removing the drill each time to allow the bits of the lock inside to fall into place.
# Put the screwdriver in the same way you would put your key in, it doesn't have to go in deep because the pins are already broken.
# Use it the same way you use your key, just turn it.
#*Warning: this method will destroy your key switch and make it so anyone with a screwdriver or an exceptionally strong fingernail to steal your car.

===Method 1===
# Open the hood.

#  Locate the red coil wire. Both the plug and coil wires are located at the rear(back) of almost all V-8 engines. Four-cylinder engines have them placed on the right side, near the center of the engine.  Six-cylinder engines are on the opposite: left side, near the center of the engine .
#  Locate the battery (it's square and has two red and black cables).

#  Run a wire from the positive side of the battery (not negative!) to either the positive side of the coil, or the red wire that leads to the coil. This will give power to the dashboard, which is essential if you ever want it to start.
#  Locate the starter solenoid. On Fords, it is on the passenger-side fender well, near the battery. On GMs, it is on the starter under the steering wheel.
#  If under the steering wheel, enter the car without setting off any alarms. If it has standard transmission, make sure the car is in neutral and the parking brake is on.

#  Unlock the steering wheel by taking a flat blade screwdriver and placing it at the top center of the steering column. Push the screwdriver between the wheel and the column, then push the locking pin away from the wheel. Don't worry, you're allowed to be rough here. The locking pin will not break or set off any alarms. The solenoid should be underneath.

#  You will see a small wire at the top of the solenoid and the positive battery cable below. Cross the two different terminal that they are connected to with a screwdriver or pliers. This will crank the engine, giving you leave to drive. Congratulations.
===Method 2===
# Enter car.  Do not break into a car unless you own it and have documentation to prove it.  Be aware that forced entry will set an intrusion alarm off if the vehicle is so equipped.

# Determine if the steering column and gear selector can be overridden, if so equipped.  Serious damage to the shifting mechanism and/or steering column will result in forcing these theft deterrant mechanisms in an attempt to override them.
# Look under steering wheel.  This may require taking an access cover off.  These are usually held in place with concealed clips or #2 Phillips type screws.  Remove if needed.
# See if there is a clip or wiring harness connector in which you can gain access to the wires behind the ignition.

# Look for the two wires that are the same, usually red and strip them and twist them together.  One of these will be the primary power supply for the ignition switch, the other will be the connection for the vehicle's electrical circuits that are energised when the key is turn to the run position.  Connecting these will provide electricity for the ignition components, so the engine is able to run when the starter is turned.

# Strip about 1 inch of insulation from this pair of wires, and twist them tightly together.  Wrap with electrician's tape if available, and do not allow them to short against metal vehicle components.
# Get the ignition wire, brown in many cars, strip it about 1/2 inch, and touch the end of the stripped brown wire with the connected red wires.
# Do not twist the brown wire to the reds, just touch the wires until ignition has been achieved.
# Rev the engine enough so you don't stall and have to do this process again.
===Method 3===

This is the most effective method due to the fact that you don't need to bother keeping wires together, raising the hood, or unlocking the steering wheel.  If you hotwire it with the wires only, your steering wheel WILL NOT TURN unless you break the steering lock. The "classic screwdriver method" where you put a screwdriver in the lock and twist doesn't work because you can't generate enough torque with your bare hands to make the lock pins break off without breaking the lock off of its mounting structure, thereby rendering the car useless. Use this method instead.
# Gather materials: 1 flathead screwdriver with an insulated handle, 1 cordless drill and a small drill bit.

# Take it from an expert:  So, there is a flap at the end of the keyhole.  Position the drill on the keyhole about 2/3 of the way up and drill in about the length of a key.  This will destroy your lock pins and make the key switch able to be turned on and off without a key. Every pin has 2 sections, followed by a spring, so drill it more than once, removing the drill each time to allow the bits of the lock inside to fall into place.
# Put the screwdriver in the same way you would put your key in, it doesn't have to go in deep because the pins are already broken.
# Use it the same way you use your key, just turn it.
#*Warning: this method will destroy your key switch and make it so anyone with a screwdriver or an exceptionally strong fingernail to steal your car.

#  Unlock the steering wheel by taking a flat blade screwdriver and placing it at the top center of the steering column. Push the screwdriver between the wheel and the column, then push the locking pin away from the wheel. Don't worry, you're allowed to be rough here. *Vehicles with a computer chip in the ignition switch cannot be hot wired, the chip enables the ECM to function, and without it, the car will not run.

added: == Steps ==
===Method 1===
# Open the hood.

#  Locate the red coil wire. Both the plug and coil wires are located at the rear of almost all V-8 engines. Four-cylinder engines have them placed on the right side, near the center of the engine.  Six-cylinder engines are the opposite: left side, near the center of the engine.
#  Locate the battery (it's the thing that looks like a battery).

#  Run a wire from the positive side of the battery (not negative!) to either the positive side of the coil, or the red wire that leads to the coil. This will give power to the dashboard, which is essential if you ever want it to start.
#  Locate the starter solenoid. On Fords, it is on the passenger-side fender well, near the battery. On GMs, it is on the starter under the steering wheel.
#  If under the steering wheel, enter the car without setting off any alarms. If it has standard transmission, make sure the car is in neutral and the parking brake is on.

#  Unlock the steering wheel by taking a flat blade screwdriver and placing it at the top center of the steering column. Push the screwdriver between the wheel and the column, then push the locking pin away from the wheel. Don't worry, you're allowed to be rough here. The locking pin will not break or set off any alarms. The solenoid should be underneath.

#  You will see a small wire at the top of the solenoid and the positive battery cable below. Cross the two different terminal that they are connected to with a screwdriver or pliers. This will crank the engine, giving you leave to drive. Congratulations.
===Method 2===
# Enter car.  Do not break into a car unless you own it and have documentation to prove it.  Be aware that forced entry will set an intrusion alarm off if the vehicle is so equipped.

# Determine if the steering column and gear selector can be overridden, if so equipped.  Serious damage to the shifting mechanism and/or steering column will result in forcing these theft deterrant mechanisms in an attempt to override them.
# Look under steering wheel.  This may require taking an access cover off.  These are usually held in place with concealed clips or #2 Phillips type screws.  Remove if needed.
# See if there is a clip or wiring harness connector in which you can gain access to the wires behind the ignition.

# Look for the two wires that are the same, usually red and strip them and twist them together.  One of these will be the primary power supply for the ignition switch, the other will be the connection for the vehicles electrical circuits that are energised when the key is turn to the run position.  Connecting these will provide electricity for the ignition components, so the engine is able to run when the starter is turned.

# Strip about 1 inch of insulation from this pair of wires, and twist them tightly together.  Wrap with electrician's tape if available, and do not allow them to short against metal vehicle components.
# Get the ignition wire, brown in many cars, strip it about 1/2 inch, and touch the end of the stripped brown wire with the connected red wires.
# Do not twist the brown wire to the reds, just touch the wires until ignition has been achieved.
# Rev the engine enough so you don't stall and have to do this process again.
===Method 3===

This is the most effective method due to the fact that you don't need to bother keeping wires together, raising the hood, or unlocking the steering wheel.  If you hotwire it with the wires only, your steering wheel WILL NOT TURN. unless you break the steering lock. The "classic screwdriver method" where you put a screwdriver in the lock and twist doesn't work because you can't generate enough torque with your bare hands to make the lock pins break off without breaking the lock off of its mounting structure, thereby rendering the car useless. use this method instead.
# Gather materials: 1 flathead screwdriver with an insulated handle, 1 cordless drill and a small drill bit

# Take it from an expert:  So, there is a flap at the end of the keyhole.  Position the drill on the keyhole about 2/3 of the way up and drill in about the length of a key.  this will destroy your lock pins and make the key switch able to be turned on and off without a key. Every pin has 2 sections, followed by a spring, so drill it more than once, removing the drill each time to allow the bits of the lock inside to fall into place.
# put the screwdriver in the same way you would put your key in, it doesn't have to go in deep because the pins are already broken.
# Use it the same way you use your key, just turn it.

#*Warning: this method will destroy your key switch and make it so anyone with a screwdriver or an exceptionally strong fingernail to steal your car.  This is not a permanent fix to your problem.  It also take between 2 and 10 minutes, depending on your level of expertise, so if you want to steal a car this way, you're out of your tiny little mind.

added: {{copyedit|date=2008-09-26}}[[Image:M52TUB25 4108.jpg|thumb|A BMW standard engine. Not the most fun to try this on.]]This is a step by step guide to hotwiring a car. Hot-wiring is absolutely illegal without the owner's permission, unless the car is being repossessed. Are you repossessing? If yes, read on. If not, get out of here. There is a huge risk of electrical shock while hot-wiring, and may not work in many cases. Some newer model cars have the required components hidden so you can't reach them. Others have "kill switches," which shut down the engine so that it cannot be started, even with the key. Older model cars, that is any gas-guzzler from 2004 down, will work, but so will some hybrid and electric cars.
#'''TAKE ONE'''
# Open the hood.

#  Locate the red coil wire. Both the plug and coil wires are located at the rear of almost all V-8 engines. Four-cylinder engines have them placed on the right side, near the center of the engine, while  six-cylinder engines are opposite: left side, near the center of the engine.
#  Locate the battery (it's the thing that looks like a battery).

#  Run a wire from the positive side of the battery (not negative!) to either the positive side of the coil, or the red wire that leads to the coil. This will give power to the dashboard, which is essential if you ever want it to start.
#  Locate the starter solenoid. On Fords, it is on the passenger-side fender well, near the battery. On GMs, it is on the starter, under the steering wheel.
#  If under the steering wheel, enter the car without setting off any alarms. If it has standard transmission, make sure the car is in neutral and the parking brake is on.

#  Unlock the steering wheel by taking a flat blade screwdriver and placing it at the top center of the steering column. Push the screwdriver between the wheel and the column, then push the locking pin away from the wheel. Don't worry, you're allowed to be rough here. The locking pin will not break or set off any alarms. The solenoid should be underneath.

#  You will see a small wire at the top of the solenoid and the positive battery cable below. Cross the two different terminal that they are connected to with a screwdriver or pliers. This will crank the engine, giving you leave to drive. Congratulations.
#'''TAKE TWO'''''(reliable; it has been tested and it worked)''
# Enter car.  Do not break into a car unless you own it and have documentation to prove it.  Be aware that forced entry will set an intrusion alarm off if the vehicle is so equipped.

# Determine if the steering column and gear selector can be overridden, if so equipped.  Serious damage to the shifting mechanism and/or steering column will result in forcing these theft deterrant mechanisms in an attempt to override them.
# Look under steering wheel.  This may require taking an access cover off.  These are usually held in place with concealed clips or #2 Phillips type screws.  Remove if needed.
# See if there is a clip or wiring harness connector in which you can gain access to the wires behind the ignition.

# Look for the two wires that are the same, usually red and strip them and twist them together.  One of these will be the primary power supply for the ignition switch, the other will be the connection for the vehicles electrical circuits that are energised when the key is turn to the run position.  Connecting these will provide electricity for the ignition components, so the engine is able to run when the starter is turned.

# Strip about 1 inch of insulation from this pair of wires, and twist them tightly together.  Wrap with electrician's tape if available, and do not allow them to short against metal vehicle components.
# Get the ignition wire, brown in many cars, strip it about 1/2 inch, and touch the end of the stripped brown wire with the connected red wires.
# Do not twist the brown wire to the reds, just touch the wires until ignition has been achieved.
# Rev the engine enough so you don't stall and have to do this process again.
*Use this knowledge responsibly.
*Vehicles with a computer chip in the ignition switch cannot be hot wired, the chip enables the ECM to function, and without it, the car will not run.
*You risk causing significant damage to your vehicle if you hotwire it.
*Never leave the ignition wires twisted together when you finish running the engine.  This can burn up the ignition system of the vehicle, and will at least discharge the battery.
